description: We are a team of curious and creative minds passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. We aim to build an innovative, interactive solution that makes space science engaging and accessible. We welcome enthusiastic teammates interested in coding, web development, AI/ML, graphic design, scientific research, storytelling, and data visualization. If you love exploring ideas and building something meaningful, join us!
summary:
Beyond the Footprint — The Stories Left Behind is an interactive educational museum exploring the scientific equipment and robotic missions left on the Moon and Mars. The project features five exhibits: the Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector, Apollo 12 Passive Seismic Experiment, Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner, Spirit rover, and Opportunity rover.

Through interactive 3D-style globe exploration, mission timelines, photographs, and detailed exhibit descriptions, visitors can discover what these objects did, what they found, and what happened to them after their missions. A lunar recession calculator and interactive quiz make the experience more engaging and educational.

The project highlights an important distinction: not everything left behind is simply abandoned. Some equipment remains scientifically useful, some instruments entered standby or stopped returning data, and some missions formally ended.

Our goal is to make the scientific legacy of lunar and Martian exploration accessible, engaging, and easy to understand.
details:
Beyond the Footprint is an interactive educational website designed as a digital museum exploring scientific equipment and robotic missions left on the Moon and Mars.

Visitors can explore five exhibits: the Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector, Apollo 12 Passive Seismic Experiment, Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner, Spirit rover, and Opportunity rover.

The website combines interactive globe exploration, exhibit descriptions, mission photographs, historical timelines, and a lunar recession calculator that demonstrates the Moon's average movement away from Earth. It also includes a status guide to distinguish passive equipment, instruments in standby or no longer returning data, and missions that have officially ended, along with an interactive quiz to reinforce learning.

We developed the project as a responsive website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a focus on accessibility, visual storytelling, and usability across mobile and desktop devices.

The project's main objective is to make space exploration history engaging and accessible while helping visitors understand the scientific value and legacy of equipment left beyond Earth.
